title: National Institutes of Health Consensus Development Conference: lactose intolerance and health
authors: Suchy FJ, Brannon PM, Carpenter TO, Fernandez JR, Gilsanz V, Gould JB, et al.
funder: Conference sponsored by the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development and the NIH Office of Medical Applications of Research; cosponsors NIDDK, NIH Division of Nutrition Research Coordination, National Institute on Aging and Office of Dietary Supplements; partners US Department of Agriculture and Health Resources and Services Administration. Informed by a systematic review from the Minnesota Evidence-based Practice Center under contract with AHRQ. The statement is an independent report of the panel.
authorConflicts: Disclosures are held by Annals of Internal Medicine (msNum M10-0536); not read.
result: Adults and adolescents with diagnosed lactose malabsorption could ingest at least 12 g of lactose in a single dose (the lactose in 1 cup of milk) with no or minor symptoms; 50 g usually induced symptoms when taken without meals. Lactose does not necessarily affect the efficiency of calcium absorption, and persons with lactase non-persistence do not have substantial impairment in calcium absorption.
